questions.q: How do you turn a regular filter into a context filter in Tableau?
options: Right-click the filter's pill on the Filters shelf and choose Add to Context
Drag it onto the Marks card
Rename the field to include the word 'context'
Context filters cannot be created manually — Tableau assigns them automatically
questions.explain: Add to Context, available from a filter pill's right-click menu, promotes an existing filter into a context filter.

questions.q: What visual signals indicate a filter is a context filter?
options: It moves to the top of the Filters shelf and turns grey instead of blue
It disappears from the Filters shelf entirely
It turns red and blinks
There is no visual difference from a regular filter
questions.explain: Tableau moves context filters to the top of the Filters shelf and colors them grey, distinguishing them from regular (blue) filters.

questions.q: Why can skipping a context filter produce a genuinely wrong answer, not just a slower one, when combined with a Top N filter?
options: Without context, Top N is computed against the entire dataset first, which can return a completely different set of values than computing Top N within a narrowed context
Top N filters cannot function at all without a context filter present
Context filters only affect visual formatting, never the underlying calculation
Skipping a context filter always doubles the row count with no other effect
questions.explain: "Top 5 within Furniture" and "Top 5 overall, then see which are Furniture" are different questions — a context filter changes which is actually being asked.

questions.q: In the example from this lesson, what does adding Category: Furniture to context accomplish?
options: It ensures a subsequent Top N Sub-Category filter is computed only among Furniture's own sub-categories, not the entire dataset
It permanently deletes all non-Furniture rows from the data source
It converts the Category filter into a calculated field
It has no effect on any other filter in the view
questions.explain: Once Category: Furniture is a context filter, every other filter — including a Top N on Sub-Category — operates only on the rows that survived it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where do context filters fit in Tableau's actual filter order of operations (covered fully next lesson)?
options: Early — before dimension filters, measure filters, and table calculation filters
Last, after every other filter type
Context filters are not part of the order of operations at all
They run at the exact same time as measure filters, in parallel
questions.explain: Context filters are computed early, before dimension filters, measure filters, and table calculation filters — Lesson 31 lays out the full sequence.
